subject: Senate majority leader
query: how is the senate majority leader chosen
title: How is the Senate majority leader chosen? A secret party vote
answer: The Senate majority leader is not elected by the full Senate. Senators of the majority party pick their leader in a closed party conference, by secret ballot when the race is contested, and the winner needs a majority of the votes cast. The Constitution does not mention the post. After the 2026 midterms, the Democratic vote is expected in early December.
body:
Under the Senate Democratic Conference's rules, leadership elections can be held no earlier than December before a new Congress begins, or whenever a vacancy occurs. Contested races are decided by secret ballot and must be held in person; voting continues until one candidate wins a majority of members present and voting, and with more than two candidates the lowest finisher drops off after each ballot. No vote of the full Senate is needed to confirm the result.

On Nov. 4, 2026, Chuck Schumer said, "I'll be reelected as majority leader," Roll Call reported. Roll Call said Democrats would hold 54 to 56 seats and that the leadership vote, which includes senators-elect, will likely happen in early December. Roll Call also reported that several Democratic Senate candidates, including Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan and Illinois' Juliana Stratton, have said they would not back Schumer.

The new Congress, and the new Senate majority, begins on Jan. 3, 2027. The majority leader sets the Senate's floor schedule and decides which bills come up for a vote.
in_the_news: Democrats won control of the Senate in the Nov. 3, 2026, midterms, and some Democratic Senate candidates have said they will not back Chuck Schumer for leader.

faq.q: Who votes for the Senate majority leader?
faq.a: Only the senators of the majority party, including senators-elect, in a closed party meeting.

faq.q: Is the Senate majority leader vote secret?
faq.a: Yes. Contested leadership elections in the Democratic Conference are held by secret ballot.

faq.q: When will Senate Democrats pick their leader?
faq.a: Roll Call reported the vote will likely be in early December 2026; the conference's rules do not allow it before December.

faq.q: Is the majority leader in the Constitution?
faq.a: No. The post was created by the parties; the Constitution names only the vice president and the president pro tempore as Senate officers.
